_about: Road-closure stress tests (scripts/fetch_stress_routes.py). Each closure is a polyline barrier along the highway's Hawaiʻi DOT HPMS centreline, within half_km of the route point nearest each anchor. Areas on the same island within radius_km of an anchor are routed (one request per area). Anchors are team assumptions: places where the highway has closed or is exposed (cliffs, single bridges, coastal stretches); the test asks what happens if that stretch is closed, not whether it will close.

closures.name: Honoapiʻilani Highway (Route 30) at the Pali and at Olowalu
closures.why: Only coastal highway between West Maui and Central Maui; the Pali stretch is exposed to rockfall and the Olowalu stretch to wildfire and coastal flooding (team assumption).

closures.name: Hāna Highway (Route 360) near Keʻanae
closures.why: Narrow road with many one-lane bridges and landslide-prone cliffs (team assumption).

closures.name: Kamehameha Highway (Route 83) at Waimea Bay, North Shore
closures.why: Single coastal road along the North Shore, exposed to high surf and flooding at Waimea (team assumption).

closures.name: Kūhiō Highway (Route 560) near the Hanalei bridge
closures.why: Only road to Hanalei and the North Shore beyond it; one-lane bridge and flood-prone valley floor (team assumption).

closures.name: Māmalahoa Highway (Route 11) in Kaʻū, between Pāhala and Punaluʻu
closures.anchor_source: Hawaiʻi DOT surveyed mile marker, Route 11 MP 53.9
closures.why: The only highway through Kaʻū; lava, earthquake and flood exposure (team assumption).
